goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: URI(website.to_s).host returns nil for scheme-less websites (e.g. www.example.com), causing website_name to be nil and the template to hide the website link entirely — a regression from the old client-side parsing

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `website_name` nil when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil (scheme-less URLs), and the template now hides the link when `model.website_name` is falsy. However, the removed client-side logic also returned `website.split("/")[2]`, which is `undefined` for scheme-less inputs like `www.example.com`, and the template previously hid the link on `{{#if websiteName}}` as well. So the claim that this is a regression from the old parsing is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Removal of websiteName computed property may break other templates (e.g. user card) that reference it, rendering empty values — unverified from the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `websiteName` from `controllers/user.js.es6`, but it also updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name` and adds `website_name` to `UserSerializer` with specs. The finding claims other templates (e.g., user card) may still reference `websiteName`, but no such references are shown in the provided diff, so the breakage is speculative and not verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Case-sensitive host comparison (== and ends_with?) causes URLs like http://Example.com/user on instance example.com to display only 'Example.com' instead of 'Example.com/user'

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, host matching uses case-sensitive comparisons (`website_host == discourse_host` and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). Since `URI(website).host` can preserve the original casing (e.g., `"Example.com"`), an instance hostname like `"example.com"` will not match, causing the method to fall through to returning just `website_host` (no path) instead of `website_host + path` for same/parent-domain cases. This matches the reported behavior for `http://Example.com/user` on `example.com`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: URI(...).host strips ports, so http://example.com:8080/path on instance example.com shows 'example.com/path' while the href retains the port, making display and link target disagree

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the display string is built from `URI(website.to_s).host` plus `URI(...).path` in several cases. Ruby’s `URI(...).host` omits the port, while the actual link in the template uses `model.website` (full URL, including any port). So for `http://example.com:8080/path` on an `example.com` instance, `website_name` would render as `example.com/path` but the href would still target `http://example.com:8080/path`, creating a real display/link mismatch introduced by this change (old JS `split('/')[2]` would have preserved `example.com:8080`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare `rescue nil` in website_name swallows all exceptions during URI host parsing, silently converting unexpected errors to no website name shown

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `website_name` with `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`, which will catch any exception raised during `URI(...).host` evaluation (not just `URI::InvalidURIError`) and then `return if website_host.nil?`, resulting in `website_name` being omitted. This does indeed silently swallow unexpected errors, but it’s more of an error-handling/observability concern than a clearly verifiable functional defect in the diff (it may be intentional to avoid serializer failures on malformed URLs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times with only the first parse guarded, an error-handling smell from duplicated parsing

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is indeed called multiple times (`.host` once with `rescue nil`, and `.path` later), but the later calls only run after `website_host` is computed and `return if website_host.nil?` short-circuits the method when parsing fails. If the first `URI(...)` parse succeeds, re-parsing the same string will also succeed deterministically, so there’s no verifiable defect or meaningful error-handling gap introduced by the diff—just minor duplication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name is inconsistent with website_name: a schemeless website like 'example.com/foo' causes website_name to return nil even though website is present, so the inclusion hint promises an attribute that can be nil

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, but `website_name` can return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` is `nil` (e.g., schemeless inputs like `example.com/foo` parse without a host). That makes the include predicate inconsistent with the actual attribute value, potentially emitting `website_name: null` even though it’s “included”. The diff doesn’t show normalization that prevents schemeless URLs, so the mismatch is real, but it’s more of an API/edge-case consistency issue than a clearly broken behavior in the shown UI (template guards on `model.website_name`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the multi-label sibling-domain branch of website_name (www.example.com on forum.example.com matching and non-matching cases), which is error-prone due to [1..-1] slice comparison breaking for hosts like a.b.c.example.com

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including a specific sibling-subdomain branch: `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` with a `[1..-1]` comparison to handle cases like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`. The added spec covers (1) different domains, (2) exact same domain, and (3) website domain being parent of instance domain (`forums.example.com` -> `example.com/user`), but it does not exercise the sibling-subdomain branch (matching and non-matching). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing test for newly added, potentially fragile logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid/unparseable website URL (e.g. bare domains like example.com without scheme) yields nil website_name, so the globe/link block renders nothing — a behavioral regression for existing user data — with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `website_name` nil when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil (e.g., a bare domain without scheme), and the template now gates rendering on `{{#if model.website_name}}`. However, the previous implementation also gated on `websiteName` computed as `website.split("/")[2]`, which would likewise be `undefined` for bare domains like `example.com`, so the globe/link block would not have rendered then either. The claimed behavioral regression for existing scheme-less website data is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side websiteName computed removed and template now depends on serialized model.website_name with no JS tests; serializers not including the untrusted attribute for certain scopes will silently render nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` in `user_serializer.rb` and implements `website_name` plus `include_website_name` (included when `website.present?`). The template change from `websiteName` to `model.website_name` is therefore backed by the serializer, and Ruby specs were added to cover the new logic. The claim that serializers “not including the untrusted attribute for certain scopes will silently render nothing” is not shown in this diff, and the “no tests” part is contradicted by the added serializer spec coverage (even if there are no JS tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name only checks website.present?, but website_name returns nil when URI(website).host is nil (e.g. scheme-less input), so the globe icon and link silently disappear despite website being populated

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, but `website_name` can still return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` is `nil` (e.g. unparseable/scheme-less strings). That means the serializer may include a `website_name` attribute with a null value even though `website` is populated. The template guards on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so in those cases the globe/link won’t render despite `model.website` being set. This is a real edge-case consistency issue in the new server-side `website_name` logic, though the diff alone doesn’t prove such inputs occur in practice or that this is a regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Second URI(website.to_s).path re-parse duplicates the first parse; duplicated parse calls are fragile and could diverge silently on future changes

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the code parses `URI(website.to_s)` to get `host`, then re-parses `URI(website.to_s)` again to get `.path` in multiple branches (e.g., `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/robustness concern: duplicated parsing can become inconsistent if the parsing logic or input handling changes, and it’s unnecessary overhead. It’s not a functional defect as shown, but it’s a legitimate review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host-matching heuristic (dropping first label, requiring equal label counts) produces false same-site positives for multi-label public suffixes like .com.au or .co.uk, letting an attacker make off-site links look affiliated with the forum

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “drop first label if same label-count” branch only changes whether the displayed value is `website_host` vs `website_host + path`—it never replaces or hides the actual `website_host` extracted via `URI(...).host`. Even if the heuristic mishandles multi-label public suffixes, the rendered `model.website_name` in the template will still contain the attacker-controlled host, so the diff does not show a way to make an off-site link appear affiliated by masking its domain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed websiteName computed property from controllers/user.js.es6 may have other consumers; Ember templates referencing missing computed properties silently render blank, needs repo-wide grep verification

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, all shown consumers of `websiteName` are updated: the `websiteName` computed property is removed from `controllers/user.js.es6`, and the only template usage in `templates/user/user.hbs` is changed from `{{websiteName}}` / `{{#if websiteName}}` to `{{model.website_name}}` / `{{#if model.website_name}}`. The finding claims there may be other consumers elsewhere, but that is not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: website_name depends on Discourse.current_hostname which varies per request, so cached/reused serialized user JSON can inconsistently flip between host-only and host+path rendering across contexts

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UserSerializer#website_name` explicitly depends on `Discourse.current_hostname` (see `def website_name`), so the same user+website can serialize to different `website_name` values depending on the request’s hostname (host-only vs host+path). The finding’s specific claim about “cached/reused serialized user JSON” isn’t shown in this diff, so the concrete inconsistency only becomes a problem if such caching exists elsewhere, but the request-dependent serialization behavior is real and newly introduced here.
